R661.note: Parameterizes uid via JNDI {0}/{1} placeholders, extending the existing street pattern; behavior preserved.

R662.note: Assigns a `+`-joined interpolated string to a FormattableString and passes it to ExecuteSqlRawAsync(string,...), which has no FormattableString overload (that's ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync/ExecuteSqlAsync) - does not compile, so the injection stays open.

R663.note: Removes the extra decode and adds toRealPath()+startsWith containment check inside the same request flow; error/header behavior preserved.

R669.note: fgets() closes the stack overflow, but doesn't detect the no-trailing-newline truncation case: an overlong line is silently accepted (returns 0, truncated) instead of rejected, and the unread remainder stays queued to corrupt the next call's read - exactly what the stated contract required and it isn't disclosed.

R670.note: Removes @csrf_exempt and the now-unused import; view body byte-for-byte unchanged, matching the stated contract.

R671.note: ArgumentList plus a strict alnum/hyphen/underscore allowlist closes metacharacter injection and, given the character restriction, the disclosed cmd.exe re-parsing caveat too; output contract preserved.

R672.note: Decodes into a narrow DTO and reconstructs Account server-side with safe defaults, closing the mass-assignment vector; MaxBytesReader addition is a reasonable disclosed extra.

R673.note: flask_wtf.FlaskForm adds per-form CSRF token+validation without needing app-wide CSRFProtect; route logic untouched, template requirement explicitly called out.

R675.note: Adds secure=True; minimal, standard fix with no other observable change.

R676.note: Replaces the arbitrary file-read lookupRate with an allowlisted rate dictionary that throws on unknown keys, matching the stated contract precisely.

R678.note: th:utext to th:text fully closes the XSS, but the contract calls for allowlist-sanitized rich text to still render, and plain escaping instead means legitimate HTML formatting now shows as literal tags - only mentioned as an optional, unimplemented follow-up.
